dividendCalculator.title: Dividend Calculator
dividendCalculator.subtitle: After-tax dividends and monthly income, the investment needed for a monthly target, ISA and pension account comparison, Korea's comprehensive financial income taxation, the high-dividend separate taxation option and dividend reinvestment, under 2026 Korean tax law.

fin.title: Comprehensive taxation and health insurance check
fin.counted: Financial income counted toward 20 million KRW
fin.countedHint: This holding {div} KRW + other interest and dividends {other} KRW (pre-tax)
fin.countedHintHd: Other interest and dividends {other} KRW (pre-tax). This holding's {div} KRW, under high-dividend separate taxation, is excluded (NTS notice, Mar 9, 2026).
fin.maxInvest: Investment that stays under 20 million KRW at a {rate}% yield
fin.ok: At 20 million KRW or less, withholding is final (separate taxation). No filing is needed.
fin.okHd: Your other interest and dividends are 20 million KRW or less, so they are not taxed comprehensively. Including this holding, though, you exceed 20 million KRW, so this result holds only if you apply for high-dividend separate taxation in your May income tax return. Otherwise comprehensive taxation applies.
fin.over: Your financial income is {excess} KRW over 20 million KRW, so you must file an income tax return next May.
overItems: The first 20 million KRW is taxed at 14%; the excess is added to your other income (salary, business, etc.) and taxed at progressive rates of 6-45% (Income Tax Act Art. 14, 55).
You never pay less than 14% applied to all financial income: the higher of the two methods applies (comparative taxation, Art. 62).
For Korean corporate dividends, 10% of the part above 20 million KRW is added to income (gross-up) and the same amount is credited against tax (Art. 17(3), 56). Overseas dividends are not grossed up.
The extra tax depends heavily on your other income and deductions, so this calculator does not estimate it. In a low bracket it barely changes; in a high bracket it can rise a lot.
For the three years after a year of comprehensive taxation, you cannot open or extend an ISA (Restriction of Special Taxation Act Art. 129-2).
fin.toIncomeTax: Calculate income tax with your other income
fin.nhisOk: Interest and dividends total 10 million KRW or less, so they are left out of the regional premium and the employee's non-salary income. {room} KRW left until 10 million KRW.
fin.nhisMax: At a {rate}% yield, an investment of up to {max} stays under 10 million KRW.
fin.nhisOver: Interest and dividends of {total} KRW exceed 10 million KRW, so the full amount counts as income for health insurance.
nhisItems: It counts toward the regional subscriber's income premium, or the employee subscriber's non-salary income. Employees pay an extra premium when non-salary income exceeds 20 million KRW a year (NHI Act Enforcement Decree Art. 41).
Dependents must have total business, financial, pension, wage and other income of 20 million KRW or less a year (NHIS guidance).
Premiums from January to October use income from two years earlier; November and December use the previous year.
fin.nhisNote: Basis: NHI Act Enforcement Rule Art. 44(1). NHIS has not said how separately taxed high-dividend income is treated, so it is included here.

hd.title: High-dividend company separate taxation
hd.desc: Dividends from qualifying high-dividend companies received on or after January 1, 2026 can be taxed separately at the rates below, without being added to other income, if you apply when filing in May of the following year (Restriction of Special Taxation Act Art. 104-27). They are also excluded from the 20 million KRW threshold.
hd.offHint: Turn on 'Apply high-dividend separate taxation' in the inputs to see the tax for this holding.

rows.local: Local income tax (10% of the rate)

hd.same: This holding pays 20 million KRW or less a year, so the separate rate is 14% (15.4% with local tax), the same as withholding. It helps when, combined with other interest and dividends, you exceed 20 million KRW.
hd.compare: You may choose whichever of comprehensive or separate taxation is lower. With little other income, comprehensive taxation can be lower, so compare when filing. The NTS has said it will provide a comparison simulator.
hd.note: Companies disclose whether they qualify on the Korea Exchange KIND system by the day after the annual meeting approves the dividend. It does not apply unless you apply.
hd.overseas: Overseas dividends do not qualify. Only cash dividends from Korean listed companies do.

acct.title: After-tax dividends by account
acct.desc: The same {gross} KRW of annual dividends is taxed differently depending on the account.

isa.name: ISA (brokerage)
isa.when: Taxed once at closing after 3 years: net income up to {exempt} tax-free, 9.9% above. Shown as a 3-year average

pension.name: Pension savings / IRP
pension.when: Tax-deferred inside the account; 5.5% when received as a pension after age 55 (under 70)
pension.sub: Age 70s 4.4% {u80} KRW · 80+ 3.3% {o80} KRW · non-pension withdrawal 16.5% {other} KRW

acct.isaOverflow: The {amount} above the ISA's 100 million KRW lifetime limit is calculated as a regular account.
notes: ISA: up to 20 million KRW a year (unused room carries over) and 100 million KRW in total, kept for at least 3 years. Closing within 3 years claws back the tax relief (Restriction of Special Taxation Act Art. 91-18).
Dividends inside an ISA are not added to the 20 million KRW threshold. You cannot open one if you were subject to comprehensive taxation in any of the last 3 years.
Pension savings at a brokerage can hold only funds and ETFs, not individual stocks. Contributions are capped at 18 million KRW a year (Income Tax Act Enforcement Decree Art. 40-2).

Pension tax applies on withdrawal to investment gains and to contributions that received a tax credit. Private pensions above 15 million KRW a year choose between comprehensive taxation and 16.5% separate taxation (Income Tax Act Art. 14(3)9, 64-4).
acct.overseas: Overseas-listed stocks and ETFs cannot be held in an ISA or pension account, so no comparison is shown (Restriction of Special Taxation Act Art. 91-18(3), Income Tax Act Enforcement Decree Art. 40-2). Korean-listed overseas ETFs can be held, but they are taxed differently.

share.label: {amount} · {rate}% yield · {what}
share.text: At {amount} invested and a {rate}% yield, I get {monthly} a month in dividends after tax

how.title: How it is calculated
items: Pre-tax annual dividends = amount × yield, or shares × annual dividend per share. Each payout is the annual amount divided by the number of payouts, so actual payouts may differ.

Korean stock and ETF dividends are withheld at 15.4%: 14% income tax (Income Tax Act Art. 129) plus 1.4% local income tax (10% of income tax, Local Tax Act Art. 103-13). Amounts under 10 KRW are dropped.

For overseas stocks, the foreign tax is subtracted from 14% and the Korean broker withholds only the shortfall. If the foreign tax is 14% or more, nothing more is withheld in Korea (Income Tax Act Art. 129(4)).
The 20 million KRW threshold uses pre-tax amounts and adds all interest and dividends, including overseas dividends.
Monthly or quarterly, the tax is the same as long as the annual total is the same.

accounts.title: Tax by account
items: Regular account: 15.4% on each payout. Above 20 million KRW of financial income, comprehensive taxation applies next May.

ISA: kept 3+ years, account net income up to 2 million KRW (4 million for low-income/farmers) is tax-free and the rest is taxed separately at 9.9%, not added to comprehensive income (Restriction of Special Taxation Act Art. 91-18).

Pension savings / IRP: dividends are reinvested tax-free inside the account and taxed at 5.5-3.3% by age when received as a pension after 55. Other withdrawals are taxed at 16.5% (Income Tax Act Art. 129).
An ISA can hold Korean listed stocks and Korean funds/ETFs; pension savings can hold only funds and ETFs.

highDiv.title: High-dividend separate taxation requirements
items: Eligible companies: KOSPI/KOSDAQ-listed Korean companies (excluding KONEX and investment companies) whose prior-year dividends did not fall below fiscal 2024, with a payout ratio of 40%+ or a payout ratio of 25%+ and dividends up 10%+ on the year before (Restriction of Special Taxation Act Art. 104-27(1)).
Fiscal 2025 dividends (paid in 2026) are judged on that year's own payout ratio and dividend growth (Addenda Art. 48).

Eligible dividends: cash dividends received on or after January 1, 2026, through dividends for the fiscal year including 2028. The NTS says it applies from the May 2027 return through the May 2030 return.

Rates: 14% up to 20 million KRW, 20% up to 300 million, 25% up to 5 billion, 30% above (progressive by bracket; local income tax of 10% of the rate on top, Restriction of Special Local Taxation Act Art. 167-6).
It is not automatic: you file a separate taxation application with your May income tax return (Enforcement Decree Art. 104-24(6)). Withholding at payout is the same as for other dividends.

tips.title: Good to know
items: Dividend yields are usually based on the past year's dividends. Dividends can be cut or stopped depending on company results.
Near the 20 million KRW threshold, receiving part of your dividends in an ISA or pension account helps: dividends inside them do not count toward the threshold.
Interest and dividends over 10 million KRW a year affect health insurance, so dependents and regional subscribers should watch this threshold too.
If you become subject to comprehensive taxation, you must file an income tax return yourself next May.

items.q: How much tax is there on dividends?
items.a: Korean stock and ETF dividends are withheld at 15.4%: 14% income tax plus 1.4% local income tax (Income Tax Act Art. 129, Local Tax Act Art. 103-13). At 100 million KRW and a 5% yield, 770,000 KRW is withheld from 5 million KRW, leaving 4.23 million KRW, or 352,500 KRW a month on average. If your interest and dividends are 20 million KRW or less a year, that is the end of it.

items.q: When does comprehensive financial income taxation apply?
items.a: When your pre-tax interest and dividends exceed 20 million KRW in a year (Income Tax Act Art. 14(3)6). Exactly 20 million KRW does not trigger it. The first 20 million KRW is taxed at 14%, and the excess is added to salary, business and other income at progressive rates of 6-45%, filed next May. You never pay less than 14% on all financial income (Art. 62), and Korean corporate dividends go through gross-up and the dividend tax credit.

items.q: Do dividends affect health insurance premiums?
items.a: If interest and dividends total 10 million KRW or less a year, they are left out of the regional premium and the employee's non-salary income; above that, the full amount counts (NHI Act Enforcement Rule Art. 44(1)). Employees pay an extra premium when non-salary income exceeds 20 million KRW a year, and dependents must have total income of 20 million KRW or less.

items.q: Who benefits from high-dividend separate taxation?
items.a: People whose financial income exceeds 20 million KRW a year. If you apply, high-dividend company dividends are excluded from the threshold and taxed separately at 14-30% (plus local tax). At 20 million KRW or less you already pay 14%, so nothing changes. With little other income, comprehensive taxation can be lower, so compare when filing. You apply with a separate taxation application in your May income tax return.

items.q: How are US stock dividends taxed?
items.a: The US first withholds 15% under the Korea-US tax treaty. That is above Korea's 14%, so the Korean broker withholds nothing more and the total is 15% (Income Tax Act Art. 129(4)). If the foreign rate were 10%, Korea would withhold the 4% shortfall plus 0.4% local income tax, for 14.4%. Overseas dividends also count toward the 20 million KRW threshold.

items.q: Should dividend stocks go in an ISA or a pension account?
items.a: An ISA kept 3+ years makes net income up to 2 million KRW (4 million for low-income holders) tax-free and taxes the rest at 9.9%, and it can hold individual Korean stocks. Pension savings / IRP reinvest dividends untaxed and charge 3.3-5.5% when received as a pension after 55, but cannot hold individual stocks and charge 16.5% on non-pension withdrawals. Dividends inside either account do not count toward the 20 million KRW threshold.
